system.name: LiteSwitch
system.one_liner: a hardware/software mechanism that harvests sub-microsecond CXL memory stalls by swapping in another thread with minimal context switching

content.subject: how LiteSwitch detects an L1 miss to CXL memory and swaps in a bundled thread via a same-address-space jump

steps.what: the runqueue's threads are formed into a bundle (Thread A + Thread B) so scheduling policy is enforced
Thread A's load at rip=0x9204 is looked up in the cache and misses
the physical address is routed; the target resides on CXL, not DDR
a same-address-space jump redirects execution into the LiteSwitch handler
the bitmap is populated with a runtime base-address mapping (e.g., 0x8000)
offline disassembly of prog extracts function boundaries into the xstate dump used to build the bitmap
the handler looks up rip=0x9204 in the bitmap to check whether xstate is needed
a minimal context switch (GPR save/restore only, xsave/xrstor skipped) selects Thread B
the CXL access proceeds asynchronously in hardware while Thread B runs
after harvesting, the bundle is dismantled back into the runqueue

content.key_idea: A cache-detected CXL-bound stall on Thread A is redirected, within the same address space and with a minimal xstate-skipping context switch, into a pre-bundled Thread B.
content.reading_order: Start at the 0x9204 load in Hardware LDMB, follow the cache-miss and routing arrows up into the Software Handler, then to Offline Xstate Analysis and Software Bundling.

summary: Figure 2 walks through one stall-harvesting event in LiteSwitch's architecture, tracing ten lettered steps across four regions. In 'Software Bundling,' the runqueue forms (B1) and later dismantles (B2) a bundle holding Thread A and Thread B so scheduling policy still applies. When Thread A's load at rip=0x9204 misses the cache (L1) inside 'Hardware LDMB,' the Memory controller routes the physical address to CXL rather than DDR (L2) and triggers a same-address-space jump (L3) into the 'Software Handler.' There, the handler's bitmap lookup for rip=0x9204 (H2), built at runtime (H1) from an offline disassembly of the program's function boundaries (X1), confirms no xstate save is needed, so a minimal context switch (H3) selects Thread B, which keeps running while the CXL access completes asynchronously (L4).
